SMTO-GWT-0017 — SMTO couldn't prepare a request for the Gateway

GUID: 5f5f4ee7-1a28-4e38-947b-01870009788a
Slug: gateway-request-body-unsupported
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gateway

What happened

  • SMTO built a request in a form it couldn't securely sign, so it stopped before sending anything to the computer. This is a problem inside SMTO, not something you did.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Technical details in this panel and select Copy error details. The details show which kind of request SMTO couldn't prepare.
  2. Write down what you were doing when this appeared, such as which task or which action on which Gateway. This helps the person fixing SMTO make the problem happen again and confirm the fix.
  3. Check the server updates section under Settings › Setup and install an SMTO update if one is offered. A newer SMTO may already include the fix for this request.

What success looks like

  • After the fix or update, the same action finishes on the Gateway without this message.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied details and your notes to the person who installed or manages SMTO. Don't keep repeating the same action; it will stop the same way each time.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Server's authenticated Gateway client received request data that was not raw bytes, so it could not sign the exact body and stopped before sending.

What this means

  • The authenticated HTTP opener received request data that was not a bytes value, so it could not sign the exact body. Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.

Why this can happen

  • The authenticated HTTP opener received request data that was not a bytes value, so it could not sign the exact body.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the request construction path and supported serialization; this is a client body-type failure, not a remote content rejection.

How to fix it

  • AuthenticatedOpener._open (agent_runtime/execution/gateway_auth.py) requires Request.data to be bytes; the calling request builder must serialize the body before authentication. Report the calling operation and Gateway path with redacted details; repeating the same call will fail the same way.
  • Correct the request builder to serialize the body before authentication; report a reproducible built-in client failure with redacted details.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The client supplies the serialized bytes that it signs and sends unchanged.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
